---
title: "02 · The arcsine law and Kendall correlation"
description: "Compute the exact probability that one comparison survives."
---

For a Haar row space, the squared projected length fraction is beta distributed.
Conditional on that fraction, a Gaussian sign-agreement identity gives an
arcsine law. Averaging yields the exact finite-`m,d` probability `p_{m,d}`.

```python
from rpgeom.laws import pairwise_agreement, kendall_tau
for m in (5, 20, 100):
    print(m, pairwise_agreement(m, 200), kendall_tau(m, 200))
```

Expected Kendall tau is simply `2 p_{m,d} - 1`. For small retained fraction it
is approximately `(2/pi) sqrt(m/d)`, which can be small even when a JL dimension
is logarithmic in sample size.
